title: LiteLLM Supply Chain Attack Hits PyPI and Docker
content_md: A new LiteLLM supply chain attack has turned version 1.107.0, an official release of the popular open-source LLM gateway, into a credential stealer. On October 21, 2026, attackers used stolen maintainer tokens to publish trojanized wheels to PyPI and poisoned Docker images, exposing cloud keys, AI provider secrets and LiteLLM proxy databases on any host that ran them. With roughly 23 million weekly downloads, LiteLLM sits inside many AI stacks, so even a two-hour window matters. This FAQ answers the most common questions about the incident and how to respond. Key Takeaways Malicious release: LiteLLM 1.107.0 on PyPI (all seven wheels) and the matching Docker images carried a credential stealer and, on Linux and macOS, an hourly remote code loader. Short exposure window: The wheels were live on PyPI from 11:39 to 13:23 UTC on October 21, 2026; Docker Hub tags stayed affected until 14:20 UTC. No import needed: Python startup hooks run the payload whenever an interpreter starts, even if the application never imports LiteLLM.
